newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end soft as worries over growth persist.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end soft as worries over growth persist.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed slightly down in low volume on Monday because investors continued to be concerned the economy would not recover rapidly after several months of slow growth, brokers said.
They added the market was likely to remain depressed this week.
On Monday, the General Index fell 1.61 percent to 1,4858.5 points and the blue-chip Selective Index fell 1.68 percent to 2,031.7 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
The government announced earlier this month that the economy grew 1.9 percent in the first nine months of the year, compared with 8.9 percent in the same period of 1995.

But investors were also disappointed the government could not yet confirm its Brady Plan deal, restructuring the bulk of its commercial debt, would be formally closed in December, as had been scheduled, brokers said.
"There is an absence of news that can motivate investors to enter the market," said Juan Palacios of local brokerage Helvetia.
Monday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru closed down 1.13 percent at 5.24 soles, on a preliminary count of 643,000 shares.
Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, which saw the sale of the state's 30 percent stake in the company start Monday, also dropped, closing down 1.70 percent to 3.47 soles on volume of 132,000 shares.
In a total of 1,072 trades, volume was estimated at 13.6 million soles ($5.3 million)
